label: Botswana self-drive: Kalahari + Moremi · Jan 12
title: Botswana self-drive: Nxai Pan, the Central Kalahari, Moremi and Khwai
summary: Self-drive 4x4 with a rooftop tent from Maun: Nxai Pan's green-season zebra and elephants, Makgadikgadi's Boteti river, 5 nights in the Central Kalahari for lions, cheetah and springbok herds, then Moremi and Khwai for leopards, wild dogs, hippos and elephants. ~$4,940 pp.
overview:
- **What this is:** a camping self-drive through Botswana in the green season, which suits the Kalahari best. The pans and valleys turn green, springbok, gemsbok and zebra gather on them, and the **lions and cheetahs** follow. Then a few nights in **Moremi and Khwai** on the edge of the Okavango for leopards, wild dogs, hippos and elephants.
- **Dates:** LAX Sat Dec 26 → LAX Tue Jan 12. 15 nights on the ground: 1 Johannesburg, 3 Maun, **11 camping in parks**, plus 2 on planes.
- **Route:** Johannesburg 1n → ✈ Maun 1n → **Nxai Pan 2n** → **Makgadikgadi (Khumaga) 1n** → **CKGR: Deception Valley 3n, Piper Pan 2n** → Maun 1n (refuel) → **Moremi (Xakanaxa) 1n** → **Khwai 2n** → Maun 1n → home.
- **Cats:** Kalahari black-maned lions and cheetah on the open pans of Deception and Nxai, with brown hyena, caracal, bat-eared fox and honey badger possible. Leopard and wild dog are best in Khwai and Moremi.
- **Hippos and elephants:** hippo pools at Khwai and Xakanaxa and on the Boteti; elephant bulls at the Nxai Pan waterhole and herds along the Khwai.
- **Herps:** the rains bring out giant bullfrogs, plus puff adders, leopard tortoises, monitors and Nile crocodiles in the Okavango channels.
- **Crowds:** almost none. Green season is Botswana's quietest time, and the CKGR may have no other vehicles at your pan.
- **The catch:** you drive, cook and navigate yourselves, on sand and black-clay mud after rain, with no fuel inside the parks. Self-drive isn't allowed after dark in the parks, so night drives only happen with a Khwai community guide (option). Carry the rental company's satellite communicator.
- **Budget: ~$4,940 pp** (≈ $9,880 for two). The vehicle is ~$1,225 pp and flights ~$2,100.

itinerary.title: Fly toward Johannesburg
itinerary.details: Qatar via Doha, Emirates via Dubai or Delta via Atlanta to Johannesburg (~24–30h). Book JNB ⇄ Maun on Airlink separately, with an overnight at JNB as the buffer.

itinerary.title: Land in Johannesburg
itinerary.details: Land, walk to an airport hotel (City Lodge OR Tambo is in the terminal complex). Sleep.

itinerary.title: Fly to Maun, collect the 4x4
itinerary.details: Airlink to Maun (~1h45, several daily). Collect the vehicle: a Hilux or Land Cruiser with rooftop tent, fridge, kitchen box, two spare tyres, a long-range tank or jerry cans, and a satellite communicator. The handover takes ~2h. Shop for 5 days of food and 60+ litres of water. Botswana is UTC+2.

itinerary.title: East to Nxai Pan
itinerary.details: ~140 km of tar to the Nxai Pan turnoff, then ~35 km of deep sand to the gate (~3h total; deflate the tyres to ~1.6 bar). Afternoon at the main waterhole: elephant bulls, springbok, zebra arriving for the rains, lions often nearby. Camp at South Camp; lions and hyenas often walk past at night.

itinerary.title: Nxai Pan's green plains
itinerary.details: Zero transfer. Dawn on the pan for cheetah and lion on the zebra and springbok; the green season is when Nxai Pan is busiest with game. Midday rest. In the afternoon, Baines' Baobabs if the track is dry (it's on a salt pan and can be impassable after rain). Puff adders and bullfrogs on the tracks after a storm.

itinerary.title: To the Boteti River
itinerary.details: Back to the tar and south to Khumaga on the Boteti River (~2.5–3h). Hippos in the Boteti pools, elephants coming to drink, zebra and wildebeest on the west bank. New Year's Eve at Khumaga camp on the river.

itinerary.title: Into the Central Kalahari
itinerary.details: Via Rakops (last fuel: fill up) to the Matswere gate (~2h), then ~1h to Deception Valley. Afternoon drive along the valley: springbok, gemsbok, red hartebeest and wildebeest on the green grass, black-backed jackal, ground squirrels, and the resident lions. In the 1970s this was where Mark and Delia Owens studied brown hyenas and lions.

itinerary.title: Deception Valley and Sunday Pan
itinerary.details: Zero transfer. Dawn loop to Sunday Pan and Leopard Pan, the best area for lions and cheetah. Midday in camp under the shade sail. Afternoon back along Deception. Watch for bat-eared foxes, honey badgers, secretary birds, kori bustards.

itinerary.title: Kalahari lions
itinerary.details: Zero transfer. Another full day on the Deception–Sunday–Leopard Pan loops, timed around where the lions were the day before. After rain the clay pans are slippery: stay on the tracks.

itinerary.title: South to Piper Pan
itinerary.details: ~2.5–3h south via Letiahau to Piper Pan, driving slowly for cheetah, gemsbok and springbok herds. Piper's waterhole draws lions; camp under the acacias.

itinerary.title: Piper and Letiahau
itinerary.details: Zero transfer. Piper Pan and the Letiahau waterhole: lions, gemsbok, possible brown hyena and caracal at dawn and dusk. The remotest night of the trip.

itinerary.title: Long drive back to Maun
itinerary.details: The long day: north through the reserve to Matswere gate, Rakops, then tar to Maun (~6–7h). Shower, laundry, refuel, restock food and water.

itinerary.title: Into the Okavango side
itinerary.details: ~2h to Moremi's South Gate, then ~2h through mopane woodland and floodplain to Xakanaxa. Afternoon drive on the lagoons: hippos, crocodiles, red lechwe, elephants, and lion and leopard in the area. Tracks can be flooded after heavy rain; check at South Gate.

itinerary.title: Dawn drive, then Khwai
itinerary.details: Dawn drive around Xakanaxa and Dombo hippo pools, then ~1.5–2h east to North Gate and over the bridge into the Khwai community area. Afternoon along the Khwai River: elephants, hippos, leopard, wild dog den areas.

itinerary.title: Khwai: leopards and wild dogs
itinerary.details: Zero transfer. Dawn and afternoon along the Khwai River and Hippo Pools. Khwai is a community concession, so off-road driving and night drives are allowed, but only with a Khwai guide: book one for the evening (option).

itinerary.title: Back to Maun
itinerary.details: Last dawn drive on the Khwai, then ~3h back to Maun via Shorobe. Clean out and repack the vehicle; return it tomorrow morning.

itinerary.title: Return the 4x4, fly home
itinerary.details: Return the vehicle by 09:00. Midday Airlink to Johannesburg, then the overnight flight home.

budget.item: LAX → Johannesburg round trip + Airlink JNB ⇄ Maun
budget.notes: Long-haul via Doha, Dubai or Atlanta (~$1,500–1,900 at Christmas, estimate) plus Airlink JNB–MUB (~$420–450 return). Price now.

budget.item: Fully equipped 4x4 camper, Maun, Dec 28 – Jan 11 (14 days)
budget.notes: ~$175/day average for a Hilux double cab with rooftop tent, fridge, kitchen and recovery kit; Dec 20 – Jan 6 is charged at high season by most firms. Split two ways. Get the zero-excess waiver and the satellite communicator.
~13–15 L/100 km in sand; fill up at Maun and Rakops. No fuel in the parks.

budget.item: Nxai Pan, Makgadikgadi, CKGR 8 days; Moremi 2 days; vehicle fees
budget.notes: P190 (~$14) pp/day at Nxai, Makgadikgadi and CKGR; P270 (~$20) at Moremi. The proposed 2026 increase to P500 was postponed in March 2026; check again before booking.

budget.item: 11 nights: Nxai 2, Khumaga 1, Deception 3, Piper 2, Xakanaxa 1, Khwai 2
budget.notes: Privately run sites ~$40–45 pp, DWNP sites much less. Book all of them before collecting the vehicle; rangers check bookings at the gate.
Self-catering in the parks; Maun supermarkets are well stocked.
$30 online for non-SADC visitors. No visa needed for US citizens.

budget.item: Travel medical + evacuation plan (no trip cancellation)
budget.notes: Make sure it covers self-drive and air evacuation from remote areas.
Moremi, Khwai and the Okavango are malarial in the rains; the Kalahari is lower risk.

budget.item: Held until the vehicle and campsites are confirmed
budget.notes: Recovery costs if you get stuck, an extra Maun night if a road floods.

alternatives.name: Guided night drive in Khwai
alternatives.description: A Khwai community guide in your vehicle or theirs: leopards, genets, servals, owls, and snakes on the move. The only night driving on the trip.

alternatives.name: Boat trip from Mboma or Xakanaxa
alternatives.description: 2 hours on the Okavango channels: hippos up close, crocodiles, sitatunga, birds.

alternatives.name: Okavango scenic flight from Maun
alternatives.description: 45–60 min over the Delta in a small plane; elephants, hippos and buffalo from the air.

alternatives.name: Guided mobile camping safari instead of self-drive
alternatives.description: Same route with a guide, cook and their vehicle. No driving, and night drives in Khwai, but well over budget.

booking_timeline.task: Price LAX → JNB round trip (Dec 26 / Jan 11) and Airlink JNB ⇄ Maun (Dec 28 / Jan 11). Get quotes from 2–3 Maun 4x4 firms for Dec 28 – Jan 11 with zero-excess cover and a satellite communicator.

Book every campsite: Nxai Pan South Camp and Khumaga (Xomae), Deception (DWNP), Piper Pan (Bigfoot), Xakanaxa (Kwalate), Khwai (Khwai Development Trust). Christmas–New Year is local holiday season and the sites are small.
Book the JNB airport hotel and the Maun lodge (Dec 28, Jan 6, Jan 10). Pay the Tourism Development Levy online.
Travel clinic: malaria prophylaxis, routine vaccines, typhoid, hepatitis A.
Check rainfall reports and road notes for the CKGR, Nxai Pan and Moremi (Tracks4Africa, the rental firm). Download offline maps.

practical:
## Entry
- **Botswana:** no visa for US citizens (up to 90 days). Pay the $30 Tourism Development Levy online beforehand. Passport valid 6+ months with 2 blank pages.
- **South Africa (transit):** visa-free; staying landside overnight at JNB is fine.
- **Yellow fever:** not required arriving from the US.

## Driving
- **Left-hand traffic.** Both drivers need a US licence; an International Driving Permit is advisable.
- Deflate to ~1.6 bar in sand; re-inflate on the tar. Never drive the parks after dark (it's illegal in the national parks, and there are elephants and cattle on the tar at night).
- **Black-clay mud** on the CKGR pans and around Nxai after rain: stay on the tracks, don't cross a wet pan, and turn back rather than get stuck alone.
- Carry 20+ litres of water each beyond drinking needs, and the satellite communicator. Tell the rental firm your route.
- No fuel in any park. Last fuel before the CKGR is Rakops.

## Camping
- Unfenced sites: lions, hyenas and elephants walk through. Sleep in the rooftop tent, zip up, never walk away from the car after dark, and keep food in the vehicle.
- Bring firewood from Maun; collecting it in the parks isn't allowed.

## Money
- Botswana pula. Cards work in Maun; carry cash (pula) for park gates, firewood and tips.

## Season
- December–March: hot days (~32–38 °C), warm nights, afternoon thunderstorms. The Kalahari is at its greenest and best for game; Moremi's game is more spread out than in the dry season, but there are far fewer vehicles.

## Health and safety
- Check travel.state.gov for Botswana before booking.
- Remote: the nearest hospital is in Maun. Evacuation cover is essential.

scores.scale: 1–5, for late December and early January. Crowds: 1 = you rarely see another vehicle, 5 = queues of vehicles at sightings (lower is better). Wildlife numbers: how many animals you see. Wildlife diversity: how many different kinds. These are judgments from how each place works in this season, not counts.

overall.note: The emptiest of the four by far, and the cheapest. You'll see a smaller share of the cats that are there, because nobody is tracking them for you.

sites.name: Nxai Pan
sites.note: A handful of vehicles at the main waterhole at most. In the rains zebra, springbok and wildebeest pour onto the grassland, and lions and cheetah follow; elephant bulls at the waterhole.

sites.name: Makgadikgadi (Khumaga)
sites.note: Very quiet. Hippos and elephants on the Boteti; most zebra move out onto the pans in the rains, so fewer herds than in the dry season.

sites.name: Central Kalahari: Deception Valley
sites.note: Often no other vehicle at your pan. Thousands of springbok and gemsbok on the green valleys, with giraffe, lions, cheetah and bat-eared foxes. Desert species only: no hippos, few elephants.

sites.name: Central Kalahari: Piper Pan
sites.note: The remotest nights of the trip. Gemsbok and springbok, lions at the waterhole, brown hyena possible.

sites.name: Moremi (Xakanaxa)
sites.note: Low season, but the Delta's best-known self-drive camp. Wet-season game is spread out, but the habitat mix is the richest on the trip: hippos, crocodiles, lechwe, elephants, lion, leopard, wild dog.

sites.name: Khwai
sites.note: South African school holidays run into mid-January, and Khwai is a favourite of self-drivers and lodge vehicles, which bunch up at leopard and wild dog sightings. Excellent for elephants, hippos and cats.

pros: Emptiest by far: whole pans to yourselves in the Kalahari.
The Kalahari's green season (big springbok and gemsbok herds, lions and cheetah on open ground) happens only now.
Cheapest of the four (~$4,940), and you set the pace.
Two very different halves: desert pans, then the Okavango's rivers.
cons: You drive, navigate, camp and cook; long sand and mud days, and the risk of getting stuck alone.
No guide: fewer cat sightings (leopards especially), and no night drives except a guided one in Khwai.
Basic or no facilities at the Kalahari and Khwai sites; carry all water.
